 :J U D G M E N T:

This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 163-A of Indian Motor Vehicles Act,
seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner is as follows:-
That on 04-10-2019 at about 01-00 a.m. (midnight), the petitioner was going towards Madya Pradesh State from Papaili village, Ananthpur District, Andra Pradesh by driving his lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-03-TE-2349 with load of Tomato.

When he reached Addakal Toll Plaza, Mahaboob Nagar district, Telangana State at that time lorry bearing Reg.no.AP-04-TU-4775 abruptly stopped before toll plaza, due to the impact the vehicle of the petitioner dashed against the said ongoing lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-04-TU-4775 further result of which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, the petitioner was taken to Virinchi Hospital, Hyderabad wherein admitted as an inpatient from 04-10-2019 to 08- 10-2019.
Thereafter the petitioner got admitted as inpatient at SVRR Hospital Tirupathi wherein admitted as an inpatient from 10-10-2019 to 06-12-2019.
In spite of best treatment he developed gangrene and underwent surgery for guilotine and amputation of left leg was done.
So far the petitioner has spent Rs.3, 00,000/- towards medical, conveyance and other expenses.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy.
He was driver cum owner of lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-03-TE-2349 and earning sum of Rs.40,000/- per month.

He has suffered pain and sufferings, permanent disability,
loss of income, loss of future income and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
3. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 - Sri.Onteru Bhaskar/the R.C. the owner of Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-04-TU-4775 remained absent hence he was placed exparte.

4. Respondent No.2 - The New India Assurance Co.Ltd.,/the insurer of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-04- TU-4775 has filed the written statement and contended that the petition is bad in law for non joinder of proper and necessary parties as the insurer and insured of the lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-03-TE-2349 are the necessary parties.

It is contended that the alleged accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner/driver of lorry bearing No.AP-03-TE-2349.
5.
On the basis of the above pleadings following Issues were framed.

: I S S U E S:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident that occurred on 04- Harinath P vs Onteru Bhaskar on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191357636/
2 10-2019 at about 1.00 a.m., at Addakl Toll gate, Mahaboobnagar District, Telangana State, due to involvement of lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-03-TE-2349?
2. Whether the Petitioner proves that he is entitled to the compensation amount claimed?
If so from whom and to what extent?
3. What order or award?
6. In order to prove the case, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and one witness is examined as PW.2 and got marked in all 11 documents as Ex.P.1 to 11.
The respondent no.2 has not adduced any evidence on his behalf.

8. Heard arguments of the petitioner and respondent no.2 and perused the material placed on record.
9.

My findings on the above-referred Issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 :- In the Affirmative.

Issue No.2:- In Partly Affirmative.
 Issue No.3 :- As per the final order,
 for the following.
 :REASONS:

10. Issue No.1 : - IN order to prove the involvement of vehicle bearing No.AP-04-TU-4775 ( here in after the offending vehicle the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and produced FIR with Complaint, translated copy of complaint,
charge sheet as per Exs.P.1 and P2.

The Pw1 in his evidence has specifically stated that, on 04-10-2019 at about 01-00 a.m. (midnight), when he was going towards Madya Pradesh State from Papaili village in the offending vehicle with a load of Tomato and when he reached Addakal Toll Plaza, Mahaboob Nagar district,
Telangana State, at that time lorry bearing Reg.no.AP-04-TU-4775 abruptly stopped before toll plaza, due to the impact his vehicle dashed against ongoing lorry , result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
11. In support of the claim and to prove the rash and negligent driving, the P.W.1 has relied upon Ex.P1 and 2 which are the police records such as F.I.R with complaint and charge sheet.
12.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by P Krishnaveni, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No.17/2020 of Mahaboobanagar Police Station for the offence punishable under section 337 IPC.

3 officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 338 of IPC.
13.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for respondent no.2 has argued much regarding the delay in lodging the complaint so also delay in filing the claim petition and submitted that the accident in question has occurred due to the sole negligence of petitioner hence petitioner is not entitled to get compensation.

14. In the light of the argument canvassed by the learned counsel for respondent no.2, if the materials placed on record are perused, the accident in question has occurred on 04-10-2019 , complaint came to be lodged on 03-03-2020 and claim petition was filed on 05-01-2022.

The wife of the petitioner is the complainant and she lodged the complaint against her own husband i.e., the petitioner stating that on account of the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by her husband the accident in question has occurred.

In the complaint it is stated that her husband sustained injuries on both legs and left leg below knee is amupted and rod was fixed on the right leg and after the surgery her husband was under bed rest for a period of three months hence she lodged the complaint at belated stage.

15. As per the averments of the petition and complaint, after the accident the petitioner was shifted to Virinchi Hospital, Hyderabad wherein he has taken treatment as inpatient from 04-10-2019 to 08-10-2019 and thereafter he was shifted to SVRR Hospital at Tirupathi wherein he got admitted as inpatient from 10- 10-2019 to 06-12-2019.
In the wound certificate at Ex.P3 there is mention about the petitioner got admitted at Virinchi Hospital on 05-10-2019.

Hence, it can be said that though the complaint was lodged at belated stage on 03-03-2020 but the petitioner has taken treatment soon after the accident on the alleged history of "RTA hit to front lorry''.

Hence, when the complaint was lodged against the petitioner alone and when soon after the accident the petitioner had taken treatment,
under such circumstances even though there is delay in lodging the complaint it would not go to the route of the case of the petitioner.

16. So far as the line of argument canvassed by the learned counsel for respondent no.2 regarding the rash and negligent act solely contributed by the petitioner is concerned, at the outset it is pertinent to note that in the petition filed under section 163-A, the question to be considered by the tribunal is the involvement of vehicle against which the compensation is sought for and not whether there is rash or negligence on part of the rider/driver of the vehicle against which the compensation is claimed.
The aspect of negligence has no role whatsoever to decide the question of entitlement for compensation.

Section 163-A of the act itself lays down that:
"not withstanding anything contained in this act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or Harinath P vs Onteru Bhaskar on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191357636/
4

the authorized insurer shall be liable to pay in case of death or permanent disablement due to the accident arising out of use of motor vehicle, compensation, as indicated in the second schedule, to the legal heirs or the victim as the case may be"
17.
In a ruling relied by the learned counsel for petitioner reported in 2018 ACJ 1 SC between United Indian Insurance Co. Ltd Vs. Sunil Kumar & Anr.

entities.text: United Indian Insurance Co. Ltd Vs. Sunil Kumar & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The question was raised whether in claim proceedings u/Sec. 163-A is it open to the Insurance Company to raise the defence/plea of negligence of victim.

It was held that "permitting Insurance Company to raise defence of negligence would bring proceedings u/Sec. 163-A at par with proceedings u/Sec. 166 which would not only be self contradictory but also defeats the very legislative intention".

18. It is not in dispute that petitioner has filed this petition u/Sec.163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988.
If claim petition is filed u/Sec.163-A of the Motor Vehicles Act, the petitioner need not prove the rash and negligent driving of the another vehicle by its driver.
It is sufficient if they prove the occurrence of the accident and involvement of the vehicle resulting in injuries.

In support of his case the petitioner has got examined himself as PW.1.
19.

In view of the above provision of law and case law, it is crystal clear that in a petition filed under Section 163-A of the Act, the proof of negligence is not required to be considered by the Tribunal.
All that has to be considered is whether vehicle against which the claim is made is involved in the accident.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P2 this court is of the opinion that the accident was occurred due to involvement or use of the offending vehicle and lorry in the accident and in that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, issue No.2 is held in the affirmative.
20. Issue No.2:-Admittedly this petition is filed u/Sec.163 -A of IMV Act.

As per the notification dated 25- 05-2018 issued by the Central Government, the following amendment was made to the Second Schedule of the MV Act:
"THE SECOND SCHEDULE SCHEDULE FOR COMPENSATION FOR THIRD PARTY FATAL ACCIDENTS/INURY CASES CLAIMS 1.
( a) Fatal Accidents: Compensation payable in case of Death shall be five lakh rupees.

(b) Accidents resulting in permanent disability: Compensation payable shall be =Rs.5,00,000/- x percentage disability as per Schedule I of the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923 (8 of 1923)} : Provided that the minimum compensation in case of permanent disability of any kind shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees.
(c) Accidents resulting in minor injury: A fixed compensation of twenty five thousand rupees shall be payable:
Harinath P vs Onteru Bhaskar on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191357636/
5 2.
On and from the date of 1st day of January, 2019 the amount of compensation specified in the clauses (a) and (c) of paragraph (1) shall stand increased by 5 per cent annually".

3. This notification shall come into form on the date of its publication in the official Gazette".
21.
According to the above notification, compensation payable in case of death shall be five lakh rupees.
Further to keep up with the cost of living in future, the compensation amount will increase by five percent annually in these type of cases with effect from 1st January 2019.
The said proviso would apply only to the cases comes under clause (a) and (c) but not (b).
22. In the present case the petitioner has sustained injuries on both legs.
As per the medical records the left leg below knee of the petitioner is amputed.
Further the petitioner has also sustained injury on his right leg.
The petitioner has examined Dr.S.A Somashekara, orthopedic surgeon at Bowring and Lady Curzon Hospital, Bangalore as PW.2 and through him OPD sheet and x-ray are got marked as Ex.P10 and 11.

The PW.2 has deposed that he examined the petitioner clinically,
radiologially for assessment of disability.
PW.2 further deposed that the petitioner has suffered disability of both the limbs at 75% and the whole body physical disability at 50%.

PW.2 further deposed that the petitioner needs surgery for removal of implants would cost around Rs.50,000/- in a private set up and he also need a sophisticated below keen prosthesis which is very expensive and runs into lakhs.

It is further deposed by PW.2 that though the petitioner has physical disability on whole body at 50% but since he stated to be a driver by profession the functional disability of petitioner would be 100%.

23. The learned counsel for petitioner referring the occupation of the petitioner and the evidence of PW.2 has vehemently submitted that the functional disability of petitioner would have to be taken as 100% because since petitioner has sustained injury on both legs and his left leg below knee is amputed he cannot continue the driving profession.

The learned counsel at this juncture has referred judgment reported in 2020 ACJ 704 (SC) between Chanappa Nagappa Muchalagoda Vs.
Divisional Manager, New India Assurance Co.Ltd.

entities.text:
Chanappa Nagappa Muchalagoda Vs.
Divisional Manager, New India Assurance Co.Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said case, the driver of truck suffered injuries to right leg in the course of his employment when the truck met with an accident.
Doctor opined that the victim suffered 37% of permanent disability to whole body.
The commissioner found that victim suffered 50% loss of earning capacity as a driver.
The Hon'b le High Court took functional disability at 60%.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court took total disablement at 100% and taken 100% loss of earning capacity by observing that Workman lost his ability to work as driver he would be disqualified from even getting a driving licence.

24. In the light of the observation made in the aforesaid rulings if the evidence on record is perused,
the accident in question has occurred while the petitioner as driver was transporting tomato load to Madhyapradesh.
Hence it cannot be disputed that petitioner is driver by profession.

When the left leg below the knee of petitioner is amputed and the petitioner has sustained injury even on right leg,
and though PW.2 has assessed the physical disability at 50% on whole body but it can be said that there is functional disability of 100% .

6 25.
Hence in view of the Gazetted notification referred above the petitioner is entitled for fixed compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-.

The calculation table stands as follows:
Total compensation : Rs.5,00,000-00 awarded 26.
As regarding liability is concerned, there is no dispute that the offending vehicle was insured with 2nd respondent and policy was in force as on the date of accident.
Further the driver of the offending vehicle had driving license to drive the offending vehicle.
Hence it can be said that all the documents pertaining to the vehicle in question was valid and in force as on the date of accident.

Hence by fastening liability on the respondent no 2 this court directs the respondent no.2 to pay compensation to the petitioner along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of accident till the date of payment of entire amount.
Accordingly Issue No. 2 is answered.
27. Issue No.3:
In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioner against the respondents u/Sec. 163-A of M.V Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioner is entitled to a total com- pensation of Rs.5,00,000/- + cost of Rs.2,000/- imposed vide order date 08-02- 2024.
The petitioner is entitled for sum of Rs.5,02,000 /- (Rupees Five Lakh Two Thousand only).
Sum of Rs. 5,00,000/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.

On deposit of the compensation amount and interest, 50% of compensation payable to the petitioner shall be deposited in his name in any nationalized bank of the choice of petitioner for a period of 3 years and the remaining 50% shall be released to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocates' fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
